chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman to whom the obituary of her husband was brought, so she observed the waiting period and remarried. Then her first husband came, so he separated from her and the second husband separated from her. How long does she observe the waiting period to be permissible to the people? He (peace be upon him) said: Three quroo' (menstrual periods). And indeed, her womb is cleared by three quroo', making her permissible to all the people.

Zurara said: And that is because some people said: She observes two waiting periods, one waiting period from each one. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rejected that saying: She observes three quroo', so she becomes permissible to the men.

key_terms.تَحِلُّ لِلرِّجَالِ: She becomes permissible to men (for marriage)
key_terms.قُرُوءٍ: Menstrual periods (used as a unit of time for waiting period)
key_terms.نُعِيَ إِلَيْهَا: Obituary/notification of death was brought to her

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who remarried after her husband's obituary if he returns alive?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the *iddah* (waiting period) for a woman who remarried based on a reported death of her first husband, only for him to return alive. He establishes that she observes three menstrual cycles (*thalathah quroo'*) to be fully purified and permissible for others, rejecting the view that she must serve two separate waiting periods. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of relying on the actual event of the husband's return to validate the previous marriage, thereby simplifying the separation process compared to other schools of thought.
